::: {.hero}
# How much does a school add? And how much does absence (or anything else) take away?

<p class="lead">Value Added v2.0 measures each secondary school in England
against what its intake and context would lead us to expect: for all
pupils, for disadvantaged and non-disadvantaged pupils, and now for girls
and boys. It is the next step from
<a href="https://adamdennett.github.io/school_attainment_tool/">How to Pull the Right Lever</a>,
rebuilt on the recommendations of a <a href="review.html">review of the
original measure</a>.</p>
:::

## What a school adds, and what absence takes away {#sec-add-take}

```{r add-take-figures}
#| include: false
wv  <- va_wide(V)
bA  <- V$coefs$estimate[V$coefs$term == "log(PERCTOT)" & V$coefs$group == "all"]
bD  <- V$coefs$estimate[V$coefs$term == "log(PERCTOT)" & V$coefs$group == "disadvantaged"]
m8  <- S$mean_att8[S$group == "all"]
m8d <- S$mean_att8[S$group == "disadvantaged"]   # disadvantaged pupils' own mean
ab  <- quantile(wv$absence[!is.na(wv$absence)], c(.5, .95), names = FALSE)
abs_yr <- yl(max(wv$latest_year))   # each school's latest full year of absence
vaa <- wv$va_shrunk_all[!is.na(wv$va_shrunk_all)]
qv  <- quantile(vaa, c(.5, .90), names = FALSE)
prop_for <- function(beta) exp(beta * log(ab[2] / ab[1])) - 1
drop  <- m8 * prop_for(bA)    # absence: a typical school -> the highest 5%
dropD <- m8d * prop_for(bD)   # the same move, for disadvantaged pupils, on their own mean
climb <- qv[2] - qv[1]        # value added: median -> top decile
short <- -(drop + climb)      # what is still missing at the end
```

Value added measures what a school does **after** its intake and context
are accounted for, absence included. So the two quantities below are not
the same thing counted twice: one is what absence moves, the other is
what the school moves once absence has already been allowed for.

```{r fig-add-take}
#| fig-cap: !expr sprintf("An average school, then the same school with absence where the highest 5%% of schools sit (full-year absence in %s, %.1f%% against a median of %.1f%%), then that school doing everything a school can do (value added %s to %s). Blue is what absence takes away, purple what the school adds back. Attainment 8 points; the dashed line is the England average of %.1f.", abs_yr, ab[2], ab[1], yl(min(V$spec$years)), yl(max(V$spec$years)), m8)
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.8
st <- tibble::tibble(
  i    = c(1, 2, 3),
  y0   = c(m8, m8, m8 + drop),
  y1   = c(m8, m8 + drop, m8 + drop + climb),
  kind = c("start", "Absence takes away", "The school adds back"),
  lab  = c("", sprintf("%+.1f", drop), sprintf("%+.1f", climb)),
  foot = c("An average school",
           "with absence where the\nhighest 5% of schools sit",
           "and doing everything a\nschool can do: top 10%"))
bars <- dplyr::filter(st, kind != "start")

ggplot() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = m8, linetype = "31", colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_segment(data = bars, aes(x = i - 0.5, xend = i + 0.34, y = y0, yend = y0),
               colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_rect(data = bars, aes(xmin = i - 0.34, xmax = i + 0.34, ymin = pmin(y0, y1),
                             ymax = pmax(y0, y1), fill = kind)) +
  geom_point(data = dplyr::filter(st, kind == "start"), aes(i, y1),
             size = 4.5, colour = DPURPLE) +
  geom_text(data = bars, aes(i, (y0 + y1) / 2, label = lab),
            colour = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 4.6) +
  geom_text(data = dplyr::filter(st, kind == "start"), aes(i, y1 + 0.55,
            label = sprintf("%.1f", y1)), colour = DPURPLE, fontface = "bold", size = 4.2) +
  geom_text(data = bars, aes(i, pmin(y0, y1) - 0.55, label = sprintf("%.1f", y1)),
            colour = "grey25", size = 4.2) +
  annotate("segment", x = 3.52, xend = 3.52, y = m8 + drop + climb, yend = m8,
           colour = WARM, linewidth = 0.7,
           arrow = grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(0.16, "cm"), ends = "both")) +
  annotate("text", x = 3.62, y = m8 + drop + climb + short / 2, hjust = 0,
           label = sprintf("still %.1f\nshort", short), colour = WARM,
           fontface = "bold", size = 4, lineheight = 0.95) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = st$i, labels = st$foot, limits = c(0.55, 4.35)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Absence takes away" = BLUE,
                               "The school adds back" = DPURPLE), name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0.10, 0.07))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Attainment 8") +
  theme_note(13) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(lineheight = 0.95))
```

Read it left to right. An average school sits at the England mean. Put
its absence where the highest 5% of schools sit (`r sprintf("%.1f%%", ab[2])`
full-year absence in `r abs_yr`, against a typical
`r sprintf("%.1f%%", ab[1])`) and it loses
**`r sprintf("%.1f", -drop)` Attainment 8 points**. Now ask it to do
everything a school can do -- to be a top-ten-per-cent school on value
added, net of its intake -- and it gains **`r sprintf("%.1f", climb)`**
back. It is still `r sprintf("%.1f", short)` points below where it
started. Being exceptional buys back about
**`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * climb / -drop)`** of what high absence
costs.

It also falls hardest on the pupils with the least room to absorb it.
The same change in absence is worth `r sprintf("%.1f", -dropD)` points
of disadvantaged pupils' Attainment 8, against `r sprintf("%.1f", -drop)`
for pupils as a whole, and from a lower base: it takes
`r sprintf("%.1f%%", -100 * prop_for(bD))` of what they would otherwise
score rather than `r sprintf("%.1f%%", -100 * prop_for(bA))`, a gradient
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * (bD / bA - 1))` steeper. Absence is not only the largest lever,
it is a regressive one.

One caveat, stated plainly because the scale of this invites
over-reading. The model is associational. The gradient says what schools
with more absence look like once intake is accounted for, not what a
particular school would gain by cutting absence by a given amount. The
direction and the order of magnitude are what to take from it. How each
number is computed from the model is set out in the
[methodology](method.qmd#sec-add-take).

## What is new in v2.0

- **Measured against intake and context only.** The Ofsted grade and the
  teacher workforce terms are out of the expectation: they partly reflect
  the very performance being measured.
- **Fairer to schools with harder intakes.** Pupil mobility, SEN rates, a
  single-sex term and neighbourhood education are in.
- **Against England.** A school is compared with similar schools anywhere,
  with the local authority's own effect reported beside it.
- **Honest about uncertainty.** Estimates are shrunk by their reliability
  and carry 95% intervals.
- **Girls and boys** have their own value added for the first time.
- **The latest Ofsted judgement** sits beside every school, including the
  new report cards.
- **Over time.** Every school has a figure for each year, so trajectories
  and moving averages over a chosen window sit beside the four-year figure.

## How the regions have moved

```{r region-years}
#| include: false
yrs_all <- va_years(V) |> filter(group == "all") |>
  inner_join(va_wide(V) |> distinct(URN, gor_name), by = "URN")
reg <- yrs_all |> group_by(gor_name, year_label, provisional) |>
  summarise(va = mean(va), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
first_y <- min(reg$year_label); last_fit <- max(reg$year_label[!reg$provisional])
moved <- reg |> filter(year_label %in% c(first_y, last_fit)) |>
  select(gor_name, year_label, va) |> pivot_wider(names_from = year_label, values_from = va) |>
  mutate(change = .data[[last_fit]] - .data[[first_y]]) |> arrange(desc(change))
```

```{r fig-region-years}
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Mean value added for all pupils by region and year, Attainment 8 points against England. ", yl(max(reg$year_label)), " is provisional (hollow point, dashed line).")
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.6
reg <- reg |> mutate(gor_name = factor(gor_name, levels = moved$gor_name))
ggplot(reg, aes(year_label, va, group = 1)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GREY, linewidth = .4) +
  geom_line(data = filter(reg, !provisional), colour = DPURPLE, linewidth = .9) +
  geom_line(data = reg |> group_by(gor_name) |> filter(year_label >= last_fit),
            colour = DPURPLE, linewidth = .7, linetype = "22") +
  geom_point(aes(shape = provisional), colour = DPURPLE, fill = "white", size = 2.2, stroke = 1) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 16, `TRUE` = 21), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) sub("20(\\d\\d)-(\\d\\d)", "\\1/\\2", x)) +
  facet_wrap(~gor_name, nrow = 2) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Value added (points)") + theme_note() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7.5), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", colour = DPURPLE))
```

Between `r yl(first_y)` and `r yl(last_fit)`, `r moved$gor_name[1]` rose most
(`r sgn(moved$change[1])` points) and `r moved$gor_name[nrow(moved)]` fell
most (`r sgn(moved$change[nrow(moved)])`). Regions are ordered by that change.
The [explorer](explore.qmd) shows the same for any area and every school,
with a moving average over a window you choose.
